inputs.xtext_rule_text:
Step returns SysML::Step :
	FeaturePrefix 'step' 
	StepDeclaration TypeBody
;

notes:
re-scoped (ADR-0015): only the kerml grammar reaches this production, so its work now lives in Step@kerml
CONFLICT: IS THE FEATURE DECLARATION MANDATORY OR OPTIONAL? The same divergence as Invariant, Expression and BooleanExpression, reached here through the StepDeclaration fragment.

READING A — the clause. KerML 8.2.5.6.2 states:
    Step = FeaturePrefix 'step' FeatureDeclaration ValuePart? TypeBody
FeatureDeclaration carries no `?`, so `step;` does not parse.

READING B — the Xtext. The pilot rule is:
    Step : FeaturePrefix 'step' StepDeclaration TypeBody
and `fragment StepDeclaration : FeatureDeclaration? ValuePart?`. Expanded, the declaration is OPTIONAL and `step;` parses.

THE CORPUS DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE HERE. A sweep of the pinned corpus for `step` followed directly by `{` or `;` found nothing: every instance carries a declaration, as in `step step1: Focus[1];`. So this production has no evidence of its own either way, and that absence is itself the reason not to decide it here. A corpus that always writes an optional thing is indistinguishable from one where the thing is required.

WHERE THE EVIDENCE IS. Invariant, which shares this divergence exactly, does have a discriminating instance — `inv { age >= 35 }` with no declaration — and it favours reading B. This unit should follow whatever is adjudicated there unless there is a stated reason to treat steps differently.

The StepDeclaration fragment is not itself the disagreement; it is a factoring of `FeatureDeclaration? ValuePart?` that would not be ported either way. The disagreement is the `?` inside it.

---
RESOLVED by adjudication, ON ANALOGY AND NOT ON A CITATION. This is the weakest of the four and is marked so deliberately.

THE RULING: FeatureDeclaration is OPTIONAL, the same as its three siblings.

KERML11-181 DOES NOT NAME THIS PRODUCTION. The issue was fetched and read in full; it names 8.2.5.7.2 and 8.2.5.7.4 and says nothing about 8.2.5.6.2 or about Step. So unlike Expression, BooleanExpression and Invariant, this ruling is not backed by a filed defect.

WHAT IT RESTS ON INSTEAD: the clause is identical in shape to Expression's, differing only in keyword and body kind; the pilot's StepDeclaration fragment is body-for-body identical to ExpressionDeclaration; and KerML 8.2.5.5.1 Connector already writes FeatureDeclaration? with an explicit '?' in the specification text, so declaration-less forms are an established pattern here rather than pilot idiosyncrasy. No semantic reason separates an anonymous step from an anonymous expression.

WHAT WOULD UPGRADE OR OVERTURN IT: a filed issue naming 8.2.5.6.2, or a corpus instance either of a declaration-less `step` or of one that requires a name. The corpus has neither today, so no oracle sweep will catch a mistake here in either direction. If this is wrong, nothing in this repository will notice — which is why it is written down at this length.
decision: A feature prefix, `step`, an optional declaration, an optional value and a type body. The declaration is OPTIONAL — BY ANALOGY WITH ITS THREE SIBLINGS AND NOT ON A CITATION. KERML11-181 does not name this clause. See the notes; this is the weakest of the four rulings and the corpus cannot check it.

evidence.note: states the production with FeatureDeclaration carrying no '?' — the defect
the pilot reaches FeatureDeclaration? through its declaration fragment, which is what this rule follows

PARTIAL MATCH ONLY, cited as pattern evidence and not as authority for this production. Fetched and read in full on 2026-09-16: it names 8.2.5.7.2 and 8.2.5.7.4 and does NOT name Step or 8.2.5.6.2, despite the identical clause shape and a body-identical Xtext fragment.
